Four days where research meets practice.
about.p1: Why Culture Matters returns to Timișoara for its third edition, 7–10 October 2026, at FABER. Over four days we bring together people who research, protect, interpret and pass on cultural heritage, to discuss the part it plays in contemporary society and the reasons culture matters.
about.p2: Cultural heritage is more than the buildings, objects, places and traditions we have inherited. It takes part in how we build identity, memory and a sense of belonging, in how we understand the past and relate to the present. And what we choose to protect, to interpret or to pass on says something about the society we want to build.
about.p3: The 2026 edition approaches these questions through three interconnected strands: Heritage under Threat, Heritage Narratives, and Heritage Literacy & Education. What happens when heritage is under threat? How do we learn to recognise it, understand it and care for it? Who builds the stories told about heritage, and how do they shape what a community keeps, forgets or passes on?
about.close: Cultural heritage is not only about our shared past; it is about how we choose to live together, in the present and in the future.
format.note: Why Culture Matters brings to the same table people who work with heritage from different perspectives, disciplines and contexts. It is a space for exchanging experience and ideas, and equally for examining concrete practice, testing methods and building new collaborations.
format.talks.label: Talks
format.talks.description: Case studies and international perspectives, in 20–30 minute presentations by the guests of each section.
format.conversations.label: Conversations
format.conversations.description: Discussions that put the guests' experiences and perspectives in dialogue, and open the conversation to the audience.
format.workshops.label: Workshops
format.workshops.description: Heritage put into practice. Eight pilot workshops of the Heritage School, for children, young people and adults, testing the methods and formats that will shape the future non-formal education programme.
theme.1.title: Heritage under Threat
theme.1.question: How do we protect heritage in times of crisis and change?
theme.1.body: War, political instability, natural disasters, climate change, abandonment, property pressure and demographic shifts put cultural heritage under threat in different ways. Sometimes the loss is sudden and visible; sometimes it happens slowly, through decay, neglect, or the disappearance of the uses and communities that gave it meaning.
theme.2.title: Heritage Narratives
theme.2.question: Who tells the stories of heritage, and whose stories are the ones remembered?
theme.2.body: How we understand a place, a building, an object or a tradition is shaped by the stories we tell about them — and by the voices we choose to listen to or to pass over.
theme.3.title: Heritage Literacy & Education
theme.3.question: How do we learn to recognise, understand and care for heritage?
theme.3.body: A relationship with heritage is formed through education, experience and direct contact with the places and stories around us. The section explores the part played by schools, museums, cultural organisations and communities in building that relationship, from formal and non-formal education to cultural mediation and participatory practice.
school.title: Heritage School
school.question: Eight pilot workshops for children, young people and adults.
school.body: Why Culture Matters 2026 marks the launch of the Heritage School, a new non-formal education initiative that starts from a simple idea: caring for heritage is something you learn.
school.more1: Not only by passing on information about history, architecture or art, but through direct contact with heritage — through observation, questions, exploration and taking part. The Heritage School sets out to develop methods by which children, young people and adults can discover, understand and build a relationship with the heritage around them.
school.more2: During Why Culture Matters 2026 the programme will be tested through eight pilot workshops, developed and led by invited professionals and educators. Alongside them, the experience and methods discussed in section III. Heritage Literacy & Education will feed into shaping the programme.
school.more3: Why Culture Matters therefore becomes the first stage of testing and development for the Heritage School, before the programme is extended in 2027.

about.p4: Through case studies, debates and workshops, Why Culture Matters puts local and international experience in dialogue — answers, methods and tools that can be put to work.
about.p5: The edition also marks the beginning of the Heritage School, a programme of non-formal education and cultural mediation that Asociația Prin Banat will develop from 2027, building on the ideas and formats tested at the symposium.
theme.1.body2: The section brings together experience and case studies on protection, prevention, documentation, emergency preparedness, intervention and recovery, putting moments of crisis in dialogue with the less spectacular but equally destructive processes that wear heritage down over time.
theme.2.body2: The section explores how heritage narratives are constructed, transmitted and reinterpreted, with attention to difficult, contested or forgotten histories, to cultural mediation, and to the part communities play in building new relationships with their own heritage.
theme.3.body2: We are interested in how heritage can become accessible, relevant and close to everyday experience, and in how the capacity to recognise, understand and protect it can be built from one generation to the next.
theme.3.more: The 2026 edition also introduces the Heritage School, a new educational initiative piloted during the symposium and developed from 2027.

register.band.note: We want Why Culture Matters to stay open to everyone, and to keep bringing guests, ideas and experience to Timișoara that are worth putting in dialogue. Your contribution helps make that possible — and it stays optional: registration is open, and free.
